summary: Iteration 14: first test of the Issue page dispatch flow, backend and frontend (web preview 390x844). Backend: 20 of 21 pytest cases pass (tests/test_iter14_dispatch.py). GET dispatch in the pick state returns <=3 picks plus current, message, timeline, eyebrow and headline. PATCH edits the message, rejects empty (422) and >600 chars (422), and returns 400 after sending. Send moves to waiting with call_at=+15m and next_at=+30m, a done event 'You replied YES. Texted X.' and a pending 'Call X if no reply.' test-reply yes moves to booked: booked_text 'tonight 7:30 PM', issue status scheduled, a good-dot event and a pending 'Text you tomorrow: how did it go?' event. no and silent move to next with the next pick and a correct prev. Sending again works. test-reply returns 400 when not waiting and 422 for an invalid reply. PUT /me/phone validation is correct (200/400/422). The Twilio webhook returns 403 without a signature. With a valid computed signature it handles host YES ('Texting High Sierra now.'), host how-it-went (outcome saved, issue resolved) and unknown numbers. Background tick was checked by back-dating Mongo fields: call_at passed -> called=True and 'No reply. Called...'; next_at passed -> next state; checkin_at passed -> 'Asked you: how did X do?'. One failing test: after the 3 shown picks all decline, the state is 'next' with a 4th hidden pick (Emerald Bay Spa Care), not 'empty'. Frontend: every requested testID renders and works. Pick layout works: #1 raised with BEST PICK, #2/#3 tilted behind, the Why #1? pill toggles why-1-text, the I'LL TEXT {SHORT} label is shown, and the message box is editable (the edit persisted and was sent). The waiting, trying-next, booked (with how-did-it-go form) and empty states all render. Empty state: notice, then Add a pro -> /bench?add=1. HostPhone save works and the form hides. No phone numbers appear in the page text, and there are no console errors. No deprecated Expo packages were found.

minor.issue: d['picks'] keeps every ranked pick (picks[:3]+picks[3:] does nothing), so after #1-#3 decline the flow moves to a 4th pick the host never saw ('Here are your 3 best', 'Picked Sierra Spa and 2 backups'). Tahoe hot tub: 4 ranked, 4 tried. Either cap at 3, or show the count and say it will try more.

The issue page also loads this payload, and it includes contractor phone numbers in bench/candidates/requests (e.g. '(415) 555-0102'). They are not shown on screen, but the brief says the host never sees contractor phones. Strip phone from this response, or stop calling it from the issue page.

The backend hardcodes America/Los_Angeles for booked_text, parse_time and event text ('replied YES for 7:30 PM'). The frontend clock() and HowDidItGo use the device timezone. On the UTC web preview the booked page shows 'tonight 7:30 PM' while How did it go says 'booked for Mon, Oct 26, 2:30 AM', and the checkin row reads 4:30 PM. Use one timezone (the property's) on both sides.
'YES 8' becomes 8 AM, while 1-7 are treated as PM. 'yes in 2 hours' parses as 2 PM.

Phone numbers don't have to be unique across users, but inbound SMS uses find_one({phone}), so two hosts with the same number get texts routed unpredictably. Host YES by SMS always approves the newest pick/next issue, which is ambiguous when there are several.

With no summary, the drafted message falls back to the generic 'The plumbing needs a fix' even when the headline is specific ('Toilet running nonstop.'). The eyebrow is likewise generic ('PLUMBING ISSUE').

integration_issues.issue: HowDidItGo shows scheduled_for in device time ('Mon, Oct 26, 2:30 AM'), which disagrees with booked-detail 'tonight 7:30 PM'. It also shows right away, although the copy says 'I'll text you the day after'.

issues: The large Screen title 'Hot tub · Tahoe Cabin' (two lines, ~46px) sits above the eyebrow 'TAHOE CABIN · HOT TUB HEATER OUT', so the rental name appears twice and the cards are pushed below the fold. The wireframe has only eyebrow + headline.
The why-1-pill touch target is 104x36, below the 44pt minimum.
The back cards #2/#3 are mostly hidden behind #1 at 390px: only a partial name shows ('High Si...', '...pa Repair'). That is acceptable for the stacked look, but the tags are cut off.

action_items: Decide on the 4th pick: cap dispatch picks at the 3 shown, or tell the host there are more backups. Currently a hidden 4th contractor gets texted.
Remove contractor phone fields from the GET /api/issues/{id} response used by the issue page (bench/candidates/requests).
Unify timezones: show times in the property's timezone in Timeline/HowDidItGo, or return preformatted times from the backend.
Make the why-1-pill at least 44px tall.
Consider dropping or shrinking the big Screen title on the issue page (rental name is duplicated with the eyebrow).
Optional: enforce unique host phone numbers. Improve parse_time for 8-11 without am/pm. Use host_note in the drafted message when there is no summary.
critical_code_review_comments: ensure(): 'picks[:3] + picks[3:]' equals 'picks'. This looks like an unfinished cap.
tick(): the state is set to 'moving' and then advance() is called with a stale in-memory issue. It works, but if advance throws, the issue stays stuck in 'moving'.
The test-reply endpoint is open to any authenticated host in production. The user approved it, but consider gating it behind a flag.
The 'No reply. Called X, no answer.' event is written at call time, before the call result is known.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows render and work

The card back stack animates in, so wait about 1.5s before checking pick-card-2/3.
rca_of_issue: 4th pick: build_picks returns the bench plus up to 3 NEARBY pros. view() slices to 3, but d['picks'] stores everything and advance() goes on until current >= len(picks).
